title: How Many Queens to BEAT A Chess YouTuber? (feat. Croissant)
summary: Collab with chess YouTuber Croissant (croissant dealer): the creator plays White with only his king plus N queens against Croissant's full normal army, adding a queen after each loss to find how many queens he needs to beat a chess YouTuber. Croissant's POV commentary is included (he says he's 'up 30 points of material' and focuses on trading queens). Croissant wins the early games; it finally took FOUR queens to checkmate Croissant.
rules: Player (White): king + N queens only, no pawns; opponent (Black): full standard army.
Start with 1 queen; after each loss add one more queen (1, 2, 3, 4).
Normal chess rules; stalemate would be a draw (Croissant worries about stalemating).
win_condition: Checkmate the full-army opponent; it took 4 queens.

opponent.name: Croissant (chess YouTuber 'croissant dealer')
opponent.avatar_description: YouTuber webcam / channel card; remake: original cartoon croissant-themed avatar (a croissant with a little face), not the real person.

board.theme_notes: chess.com green board; 'Croissant POV' webcam overlay; 'You Won!' game review popup at the end.

setup: rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/8/3QK3 w kq - 0 1 for game 1 (one queen on d1); add queens on the back rank (c1, e/f1...) each game.
events: Queen counter increments after each loss.
current_impl_issues: Legacy 'kingplus' Q vs bot 'Croissant' is broadly right; make the opponent a mid-strength human-like bot named Croissant with chatty 'trade the queens' style, and the target is 4 queens.
evidence: SRT 0:00 'finding out how many queens I need to be a chess YouTuber... hello everybody I'm croissant dealer'; 0:40 'I'm literally up 30 points of material' (Croissant POV); 1:40 'the only thing we need to focus on is trading off our Queens'; 4:50 'two queens... still up 21 points'; 36:20 'Checkmate... It took us Four Queens to defeat a chess YouTuber'. Frames: white K+queens vs black full army; Croissant POV webcam.
